claims.statement: frontend/mcm-app is a single Expo Router codebase whose app.json configures Metro's web output as "server" (not a static export) because the same process also hosts the BFF via file-based +api.ts routes under src/app/.
mcm-app and @mcm/design-system have both migrated from Tamagui v1 to Tamagui v2 (package.json pins tamagui/@tamagui/* to ^2.3.0 in both packages), reversing the earlier v1-only pin.

babel.config.js now installs the @tamagui/babel-plugin optimizing compiler plugin for every non-test build (excluded only under NODE_ENV=test so Jest still renders Tamagui at runtime), whereas the design system previously ran with only the Tamagui runtime and no compiler plugin.

The Tamagui compiler plugin lets Metro tree-shake the @mcm/design-system barrel import, which fixes the earlier problem where importing one design-system component pulled the whole Tamagui library into the web bundle and OOM-crashed Metro's dev bundler.

src/app/(app)/settings/ is an Expo Router group with a _layout.tsx that renders a shared SettingsNav sub-navigation above the active area via a Slot (not a nested Stack), because the settings areas behave as a tab row with no push/pop navigation history of their own.

The settings sub-navigation is defined by a single SETTINGS_AREAS registry (src/components/settings/settings-nav.tsx) listing Profile, Movie Assistant, Backups, Account, and an admin-only Admin entry (Account has no adminOnly flag and is placed last among non-admin rows because it is a purely destructive action); role-based hiding of the Admin entry is presentation only, and access is actually enforced by a separate ProtectedRoute requiredRole="mc-admin" guard on the admin route itself.

Each settings route (index.tsx, assistant.tsx, backups.tsx, admin.tsx) is a thin file that reports its own current_screen label via useReportUiState and renders a screen component from src/screens/settings/, so adding a new settings area is meant to require only a registry row, a route, and a screen.

The client-side Backups settings area (feature 073 / backlog #236, src/screens/settings/backups-settings-screen.tsx) lets a user configure backup destinations, create/edit backup jobs and schedules, view run history and stored versions, and manage the standing consent for unattended scheduled runs, composed from src/components/backups/ and the use-backup-destinations/use-backup-jobs/use-backup-consent hooks.

The Backups settings area's hooks call the BFF's bff-api/backups/* routes through the same cookie-authenticated src/utils/api-client.ts as the rest of the client, and a destination secret is write-only end to end — the client never receives one back, an edit form starts with an empty secret field by design, and omitting the secret field on an update preserves the stored secret server-side.

Password-manager autofill is suppressed via the NoAutoFillInput component used across most forms (collection/movie forms, search bar, assistant config), while the registration form (register-form.tsx) deliberately uses a plain React Native TextInput so autofill works there.

src/utils/api-client.ts was relocated out of src/bff-server/ (feature 077 / backlog item #566) because that path named what it talks to rather than where it runs; scripts/check-no-server-imports.mjs now enforces that src/bff-server/** is imported only by server code, preventing a repeat of a prior bug where a client component imported a server-only backup-run-summary module and shipped an unwanted luxon dependency into the web bundle.

The Account settings area (feature 076, src/screens/settings/account-settings-screen.tsx backed by src/hooks/use-account-deletion.ts) lets a user delete their own account, but only after a fresh re-authentication at Keycloak (prompt=login, max_age=0) that the BFF verifies server-side; on web the BFF builds the authorization request and owns the callback so the browser only sees a redirect URL, while on native the device runs its own expo-auth-session + PKCE flow (using a deletion-specific redirect distinct from the login callback) and posts the resulting code back to the BFF, and in neither case does the client itself perform the deletion.

Granting the Backups area's standing scheduled-run consent (src/hooks/use-backup-consent.ts) is a client-initiated, identity-provider-mediated round trip, not a local toggle: startGrant() only asks the BFF for a Keycloak authorization URL, the BFF itself records the grant after the user authenticates and Keycloak calls back, and revoke() surfaces an error and leaves the granted state unchanged (rather than optimistically clearing it) whenever the BFF reports that the identity provider refused the revocation.

SettingsNav selects an area via router.replace rather than router.navigate/push because on the app's Expo Router version navigate pushes a sibling settings area onto the navigation stack instead of swapping it, which previously left two mounted copies of the same settings screen (a testID collision on web) after switching areas a few times; the settings area list itself has no back-stack of its own.

Metro's dev transform-worker derives a `require.context(<projectRoot>, false, /\.env/)` for the virtual module `expo/virtual/env.js`, which crawls every project-root `.env*` file whose extension Metro watches while dotenv-parsing only six names (`.env`, `.env.local`, `.env.development`, `.env.development.local`, `.env.production`, `.env.production.local`); the unparsed remainder falls through to Babel's JavaScript transform, so `frontend/mcm-app/.env.e2e.local` produced a `SyntaxError: Missing semicolon` and made `pnpm web` return HTTP 500 for every request (item #242, measured 2026-09-07).

The fix for item #242 is a Metro `resolver.blockList` entry computed by `metro-env-blocklist.js` that matches every root-level `.env*` file outside Expo's six parseable names, deliberately chosen over dropping `'local'` from `watcher.additionalExts` (which would also stop Metro crawling `.env.local`, a file Expo legitimately reads); the regex must stay in step with Expo's own parseable set, and reformatting the offending file is not an option because no dotenv-valid formatting satisfies a JavaScript parser and the format is shared with bash `source`, `docker run --env-file`, and the Python `_load_env_file` helpers.

`metro.config.js` redirects the `@segment/analytics-node` specifier to `metro-shims/segment-analytics-node.js` because CopilotKit's React Native entry statically imports a telemetry client that pulls `jose`, whose Node build requires `crypto` and thus breaks the Android/iOS bundle with `Unable to resolve module crypto from jose/.../node/cjs/runtime/verify.js`; the shim is a no-op with a preserved API surface rather than an empty module, because the telemetry client constructs `new Analytics(...)` unconditionally on native and an empty module would throw "undefined is not a constructor".

`scripts/check-no-server-imports.mjs` is a keyless gate (run in the guardrails `naming` job as `--selftest` plus the real scan) that fails on any non-exempt file under `frontend/mcm-app/src` importing into `src/bff-server/`; it resolves both the `@/` alias and a relative walk, and matches import statements over the whole file rather than line by line, because the first line-based version could not see the multi-line import it was written to catch.

The server-import gate's exemption mechanism is an `@client-safe: <reason>` marker written inside the module itself rather than an allowlist entry in the gate — a bare marker with no reason is not honoured, and a marker must also be paired with an entry in `SERVER_ONLY_EXEMPT` in `scripts/check-web-bundle-budget.mjs`; no module carries a marker today because item #566 relocated the only candidate (`api-client.ts`) to the Utils-Layer, and the mechanism is retained deliberately so its tests keep documenting the rule.

`scripts/check-web-bundle-budget.mjs` asserts three separate things: the web entry chunk stays inside a committed byte budget, the deferred assistant packages are absent from the entry chunk, and server-only code (`src/bff-server/`, `luxon`) is absent from EVERY client chunk rather than only the entry chunk, since a gate reading just the entry chunk would report clean while server code shipped inside a deferred chunk.

The web security-header layer is built by `frontend/mcm-app/web-security-headers.js`, a pure plain-CommonJS module (not TypeScript) because the hand-written `server.js` Expo adapter lives outside the Metro bundle and cannot import the app's compiled TS; it builds an enforcing (never report-only) CSP whose `script-src` allow-lists Expo Router's single inline hydration bootstrap script by a stable sha256 hash so neither `'unsafe-inline'` nor `'unsafe-eval'` is needed, plus three always-on static baseline headers stamped on every response.

The browser-facing Keycloak origin that the CSP's `connect-src` needs is read from env at boot and reduced to a bare `http(s)` origin, falling back to a localhost default on anything malformed, because a scheme-less or non-web-scheme value does not throw in the WHATWG `URL` parser — it yields the opaque origin string `null`, which would emit a broken `connect-src 'self' null` directive.

The web-app CSP is path-scoped out of `/bff-api` by `isApiPath`, so the API surface keeps exactly one CSP — its own strict handler policy — rather than depending on adapter same-name header merge order, while the three static baseline headers apply to all paths.

The strict CSP's blocking of a third-party `new Function("")` eval-availability probe is a documented, accepted residual: the probe is wrapped in try/catch, the library degrades gracefully with the app fully functional, and the browser logs one benign `eval` CSP violation — `'unsafe-eval'` is deliberately not added to silence it, because permitting real eval app-wide would defeat the hardening.

`tests/e2e/web/security-headers.spec.ts` asserts the response contract across the three classes this process serves — SSR HTML, a static asset, and a JSON API response — including that `X-Powered-By` is absent from all three, and opts out of the shared authenticated Playwright `storageState` because all three are public routes.

`frontend/mcm-app/plugins/with-dev-cleartext.js` (a config plugin listed in `app.json`, run at `expo prebuild` time because `android/` is gitignored and regenerated) permits Android cleartext HTTP for `localhost`, `127.0.0.1` and the emulator host alias `10.0.2.2` only, via a generated network security config referenced by `android:networkSecurityConfig`; without it the standalone release APK the mobile E2E suite installs cannot reach the dev BFF and the login POST fails with `ERR_NETWORK`, while every other host stays cleartext-blocked so the production HTTPS build is unaffected.
